title: Sport-Arbitrage: when the odds add up

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two betting sites give odds on the same match. Sometimes their disagreement is big enough that you can bet on opposite outcomes at both and lock in a profit. Sport-Arbitrage tells you when.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Simple maths. For each odd, take its inverse. Add them up across the outcomes. If the sum is below one, there's an arbitrage opportunity.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The note has one. Site one offers 2.10 on a win, site two offers 2.05 on a loss. Their inverses add up to about 0.964. With 1,000 dollars, the stakes work out to about 494 on the win and 506 on the loss.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Either way you get back about 1,037 dollars, so the guaranteed profit is around 37 dollars. The stake split is proportional to each inverse odd, which makes every outcome pay the same.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a single web page with a form: pick two or three outcomes, enter the odds from both sites and your total investment, and click Calculate. A Python notebook runs the same formulas, so you can double-check the numbers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing at all. Just open the page. The written page walks through the three-outcome case too.
